messages:
Sam: quick one — seeing intermittent HTTP/2 RST_STREAMs from our Go client when we cancel contexts + immediately retry. using a shared http.Client with custom Transport. connections spike and we get a bunch of resets. anyone seen this pattern?

Sam: snippet of how we create the client:
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 50,
  IdleConnTimeout: 30 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr, Timeout: 0}
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
```

Rachel: are you on stdlib auto http2 (net/http) or explicitly using golang.org/x/net/http2? also: are you always calling `resp.Body.Close()` on error paths? RST is normal when stream is cancelled.

Sam: stdlib http2 automatic. we usually close body but some code paths bail on context cancel before close — and we retry immediately. tcpdump shows lots of RST_STREAM and occasional GOAWAY from the server.

Alex: common gotcha — canceling ctx will RST the stream, server may send GOAWAY if overloaded. immediate retries can make it worse (thundering herd). try backoff + jitter and avoid retry on context.Canceled.

CJordan: also check that you aren't reusing the same request body reader across retries — that can cause odd behavior. for streaming endpoints, long-lived requests should ideally use a dedicated client or separate connections.

Maria: from infra: we tuned these values in another service with similar workload: MaxIdleConns=200, MaxIdleConnsPerHost=100, IdleConnTimeout=15s, TLSHandshakeTimeout=5s. calling `Transport.CloseIdleConnections()` after a surge helped during experiments.

Rachel: small code pattern we use to gate retries:
```go
if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
  // don't retry, caller canceled
} else if isStreamReset(err) {
  // retry with exponential backoff + jitter
}
```
and `isStreamReset` just checks for known substrings from http2 or net/http errors (eg "rst_stream", "stream closed") — annoyingly stringy but pragmatic.

Sam: good call. we'll stop retrying for context.Canceled and add backoff. any suggestions for detecting stream-reset more robustly?

CJordan: you can inspect `err.Error()` for http2 err codes or check for x/net/http2 specific error types if you import the package. small helper works fine until we need something robust.

Alex: one more transport tweak — set MaxIdleConnsPerHost lower if you see per-host conn saturation, and reduce IdleConnTimeout for short streams. also ensure you don't disable keepalives (we rely on them for reuse).

Maria: note: http2 server side max concurrent streams is a factor too; if streams pile up the server will signal GOAWAY. can't tune that from client, but you can smooth traffic.

deploy-bot: prod alert: increased 502 rate from edge -> inference cluster at 15:32 UTC, correlated with spike in stream resets.

Sam: I'll implement: (1) guard against context.Canceled, (2) add exponential backoff + jitter, (3) lower IdleConnTimeout to 15s for this client, and (4) call CloseIdleConnections during cooldown. will open a PR and post perf numbers. ping me if you want to pair. :thumbsup:

Rachel: thanks — appreciate the follow up.

Alex: happy to review the PR. quick tip: add a small test that simulates ctx cancel and asserts conn counts don't leak.

Sam: will do, thanks all!
